profile.reading:
Sabey Data Centers operates SDC Columbia, a data center campus at 4405 Grant Road in East Wenatchee, Douglas County, Washington, in the Columbia River region. Sabey traces its roots to 1972, when Dave Sabey founded Sabey Corporation as a Pacific Northwest commercial real estate developer; the company entered the data center business almost by accident during the dot-com collapse, when a vacated tenant building in Seattle became SDC Seattle Building 5. Sabey Data Centers itself was formally established in 2010 as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors, a structure confirmed on both the operator's own site and independently by Wikipedia. As of 2026 Sabey operates seven data center campuses nationally, together totaling more than 3.5 million square feet and, per Wikipedia's most recent figure, nearly 400 MW of capacity; Tim Mirick became Sabey's president effective January 1, 2025, succeeding Rob Rockwood.

Per the operator's own SDC Columbia page, the East Wenatchee campus is marketed on renewable hydroelectric power priced at 5 cents per kilowatt-hour, drawn from the Columbia River hydroelectric system that also supplies neighboring Quincy, Washington's data center cluster. The campus comprises three completed buildings plus a fourth under construction, totaling roughly 70 MW of capacity campus-wide, a figure the operator does not break out per individual building. Aggregator Baxtel separately reports an additional 9 MW of Tier III-standard critical power expected at the campus from Q4 2026, a forward-looking figure not yet delivered as of this writing and not applied as confirmed capacity to any building here.

This registry entry tracks the Intergate Columbia campus generally rather than an individually numbered building. Aggregator DatacenterHawk lists individually numbered Buildings B and D at this same 4405 Grant Road street address, while a Building A on the same campus carries no separately confirmed street number in sourcing located to date; both are recorded as separate rows in this registry.

reading.body:
Intergate Columbia is a 70 MW campus in East Wenatchee, Washington, marketed on hydroelectric power at 5 cents per kilowatt-hour and operated by Sabey Data Centers across three buildings with a fourth under construction. The operator has published the total campus capacity but not the breakdown by building, so the contribution of this facility to the campus total cannot be determined from available sources. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 70 MW of campus IT load would support roughly 1,750 racks, though actual customer density may differ.

In Washington state, Intergate Columbia ranks third by published megawatt capacity among the 46 mapped facilities and represents just over one-third of the 60 MW of published capacity the state has disclosed. Only one other facility in the state publishes a specific capacity figure. The site sits in the Columbia River region with access to renewable hydroelectric generation, a power source that has drawn multiple large data center operators to eastern Washington.

Future capacity at this campus is not yet live. Baxtel reports 9 MW of additional Tier III critical power expected available by Q4 2026, but this figure is not yet delivered and therefore not applied to current capacity. The operators own site does not publish certifications or specific tenant information for this campus.
